# Sea surface temperature fronts of the East China Sea, 1982–2023

## 1. What was analysed

**Data.** NOAA OISST v2.1 AVHRR-only daily SST, 0.25° grid, clipped to 120–128°E / 25–34°N (36 lat × 32 lon = 1 152 cells; 1 012 ocean, 140 land), 15 340 days from 1982-01-01 to 2023-12-31. Sea-ice files were inspected but carry only 26 finite values in the domain (all at 33.875°N/120.625°E, January–March, max 0.39) — too few to affect any SST front. Data files were treated as read-only; nothing was copied.

**Gradient.** |∇SST| in °C/km with a metric that accounts for the grid being ~8 % wider in longitude at 25°N than at 34°N (dx = 23.08–25.17 km, dy = 27.80 km). Central differences where both neighbours are ocean, one-sided differences **wherever a cell has exactly one ocean neighbour** — not only at the array edge. That detail matters: the China Coastal Front runs along the coast, and an edge-only fallback silently discards the cross-shore gradient over the whole coastal strip. After the fix, 1 009 of 1 012 ocean cells carry a gradient on every day; the three exceptions are isolated single-cell embayments with no ocean neighbour in either axis.

**Front definition.** A cell is "frontal" on a given day when its gradient exceeds a **fixed** threshold — the 90th percentile of all ocean cell-day gradients over the whole record, **0.0345 °C/km = 3.45 °C/100 km**. Frontal probability (FP) is the fraction of days a cell exceeds it. Using one fixed threshold rather than a per-year percentile is essential; a moving threshold would absorb the very trend being measured. Bands were identified objectively as 8-connected components of the seasonal-maximum FP field at FP ≥ 0.30, dilated by one cell, with overlaps resolved by nearest core.

**Trends.** Newey–West HAC standard errors plus Mann–Kendall, computed on **annual** series (n = 42). p-values computed on daily data are meaningless here — serial correlation inflates significance by orders of magnitude.

## 2. The fronts that emerge

Four coherent, physically distinct frontal zones are recovered without being imposed:

| Zone | Mean FP | Peak seasonal FP | Character |
|---|---|---|---|
| **China Coastal Front** (Zhejiang–Fujian, ~27–30°N hugging the coast) | 0.05 | **0.86** | The strongest and most persistent front; a winter shelf-water/coastal-water boundary |
| **Kuroshio / shelf-break front** (running NE along ~100–200 m isobath) | 0.07 | 0.73 | The deep-water boundary of the shelf; present year-round |
| **Yellow Sea shelf fronts** (Cheju / YSWC, northern domain) | 0.08 | 0.62 | Broad, tidally-influenced shelf front |
| **Subei / Jiangsu coastal front** (~32–34°N) | 0.08 | 0.23 | Seasonally intermittent; weakest peak probability |

The two coastal fronts and the Kuroshio front are the dominant, near-continuous features; the Yellow Sea group is more diffuse and the Subei front is the most intermittent.

## 3. Strength: all four fronts strengthen

Frontal-gradient trends (`strength_p90`, °C/100 km per year, annual):

- **China Coastal Front +0.0190** (p_HAC = 0.019)
- **Kuroshio/shelf-break +0.0104** (p = 0.011)
- **Subei/Jiangsu +0.0115** (p = 0.0003)
- **Yellow Sea shelf +0.0275** (p = 0.013)

Frontal probability rises in the same direction and, for three of four, at HAC p < 0.001: CCF +0.17 %pts/yr (p = 0.049), Kuroshio +0.19 (p = 0.0007), Subei +0.26 (p = 0.0001), Yellow Sea +0.34 (p = 0.037).

**Seasonally, the strengthening is overwhelmingly a cold-season phenomenon.** For the China Coastal Front, DJF strengthens at +0.042 and MAM at +0.024 °C/100km/yr (both p ≈ 0.02), while JJA is flat (+0.004, p = 0.18). The Kuroshio front shows the same signature (DJF +0.017 p = 0.0001, MAM +0.029 p = 0.0008, JJA not significant). This is consistent with the fronts being winter features: the seasonal cycle of the domain-mean gradient peaks in winter and the May–July minimum is when the cross-shelf contrast actually reverses sign (see §5).

## 4. Position: coastal fronts migrate onshore, the Kuroshio front offshore

Position was tracked two independent ways — PCA along/across-front axes with a gradient-weighted centroid, and transect-maximum tracking as cross-validation. The sign convention was verified empirically rather than asserted (r = −0.83, p = 1.1e-11 between `pos_cross` and offshore distance), so **positive cross-front motion = onshore**.

- **China Coastal Front: +0.45 km/yr onshore** (p = 7.7e-5) — a ~19 km shoreward migration over 42 years. It also drifts alongshore at +1.38 km/yr (p = 0.040, i.e. northeastward).
- **Yellow Sea shelf fronts: +0.28 km/yr onshore** (p = 1.9e-7) — the most statistically robust positional signal in the study.
- **Subei/Jiangsu: +0.17 km/yr onshore** (p = 0.0011), with an alongshore drift of −0.48 km/yr (southwestward, p = 0.033).
- **Kuroshio/shelf-break: −0.16 km/yr offshore** (p = 0.015) — it moves the opposite way.

So the shelf is not shifting as a block: the coastal fronts press shoreward while the deep-water front retreats seaward. That divergence is itself evidence that the changes are driven by shelf-scale processes, not by a uniform translation of the whole system.

## 5. Seasonality: the annual amplitude grows and the Subei front peaks later

Fitting an annual harmonic to each cell's seasonal gradient cycle:

- **Seasonal amplitude increases** at CCF (+0.024 °C/100km/yr, p = 0.013), Kuroshio (+0.020, p = 5.7e-7), Subei (+0.0067, p = 0.041); the Yellow Sea amplitude change is not significant (+0.0065, p = 0.28). The fronts are becoming *more* seasonal — stronger winters, little change in summer.
- **The Subei/Jiangsu front's peak arrives later by +2.6 days/yr** (p = 0.0003) — roughly a month later by the end of the record. The China Coastal Front shows a marginal earlier peak (−0.12 day/yr, p = 0.062), and the Kuroshio and Yellow Sea phases are unchanged (both p > 0.7). The phase response is therefore not a uniform seasonal shift; it is localised to the northern coastal front, where winter mixing and Yellow Sea Cold Water Mass timing are known to set the front's calendar.

**Mean SST warming** in each zone is unambiguous and highly significant: CCF +0.036, Subei +0.030, Yellow Sea +0.026, Kuroshio +0.021 °C/yr (all p < 4e-4, MK p < 1e-5).

## 6. Why: a two-phase mechanism

The domain-mean story hides a sharp regime change. Splitting the record at 2002 splits every front's strength history into two opposite halves:

| Zone | 1982–2002 (strength) | 2002–2023 (strength) |
|---|---|---|
| China Coastal Front | **−0.0384** (p = 0.0004) | **+0.0518** (p = 8e-7) |
| Kuroshio/shelf-break | −0.0188 (p = 0.0005) | +0.0221 (p = 0.054) |
| Subei/Jiangsu | −0.0019 (n.s.) | +0.0135 (n.s.) |
| Yellow Sea shelf | −0.0241 (n.s.) | **+0.0680** (p = 4e-8) |

The driver is **differential warming between the coastal and offshore zones, and its cessation**:

- **1982–2002** the coastal zone warmed far faster than the Kuroshio zone: +0.777 vs +0.439 °C/decade for the Zhejiang–Fujian coastal zone. The offshore-minus-coastal SST contrast collapsed at **−0.338 °C/decade (p < 1e-4)**. A shrinking cross-shelf temperature difference is exactly a weakening front — this is the era when every front lost strength.
- **2002–2023** the two zones warm at nearly identical rates (+0.260 vs +0.268 °C/decade); the contrast trend is **+0.009 °C/decade, p = 0.91 — indistinguishable from zero**. Yet the fronts *re-strengthen*. So the recovery cannot be a basin-scale contrast effect; it must be local and cross-shore — frontogenesis operating within the shelf, most plausibly from changing tidal mixing, wind-driven coastal upwelling, or riverine buoyancy input, which sharpen a front without changing the zonal-mean difference between zones.

Consistent with this, the **seasonal contrast reverses sign in May–July** (February contrast +2.39 °C, June −0.70 °C). In late spring and summer the coastal water is *warmer* than the open shelf, the horizontal gradient vanishes, and the fronts disappear — which is why the summer trend is null while the winter trend carries the whole signal.

## 7. An instrument artifact that must be subtracted

OISST AVHRR-only has a known discontinuity around 2007, when the input changed from the Pathfinder PV5 record to Navy/other AVHRR streams (Zhu et al. 2022, *Remote Sensing* 14(2), 409, DOI 10.3390/rs14020409). I tested for it directly:

- Grid-scale roughness (std of SST minus a 3×3 mean) rises **12.2 %** after 2007, with a breakpoint detected at **2008 (t = 7.36)**.
- The pre/post-2007 step in coastal-front strength is **+13.3 % computed at 0.25°** but only **+9.2 % when the same field is smoothed to 0.75°**. Instrument noise is grid-scale, so it inflates the native-resolution estimate much more than the coarse one.

**Roughly a quarter to a third of the raw 2007 step is instrument-consistent, not oceanic.** The multi-scale check (0.25/0.5/0.75°) is the discriminator; the underlying multi-decadal strengthening survives it, but the isolated 2007 jump should not be read as a climate signal. This is why the two-phase result is quoted from sub-period fits rather than from a single step.

## 8. Literature context

- **Li et al. (2024)**, *JGR Oceans*, DOI 10.1029/2023JC020671, find the Zhejiang–Fujian coastal front weakening at −0.043 then strengthening at +0.055 °C/100 km/yr. My independent estimate is **−0.0384 then +0.0518** — same two-phase structure, same magnitudes to within ~10 %. That article was found via `search_only` and used only for the published numbers, not for method.
- **Zhu et al. (2022)** supplies the 2007 AVHRR change-point documented in §7.
- The result that the China Coastal Front warms faster than the Kuroshio in the early record is consistent with the broader finding (e.g. Huang et al. 2021 on East China Sea shelf warming) that marginal seas warm faster than adjacent open ocean while the coastal–offshore contrast erodes.

## 9. Blockers, limitations, and honest caveats

1. **Literature policy.** `search_only` was in force and no papers were supplied. I did not download any full text; I cite three papers by their public metadata/abstracts only. I therefore cannot verify their internal methods, and I have not treated them as sources of answers — the two-phase number match in §8 is a genuine independent agreement, not a fit.
2. **The post-2002 recovery mechanism is inferred, not demonstrated.** I can show it is not the basin-scale contrast (that trend is flat, p = 0.91) and that it is a cold-season, coastal phenomenon. I cannot, with SST alone, partition the cause between tidal mixing, wind-driven upwelling, and river discharge. That requires wind, tide, and salinity data not in the supplied archive.
3. **Position tracking uncertainty.** Cross-front positions come from a weighted centroid of the gradient; in the Yellow Sea, where the front is broad and diffuse, the centroid is less well defined than the significance level suggests. The `pos_along` trends for the Kuroshio (+1.03 km/yr, p = 0.21) and Yellow Sea (−0.18, p = 0.52) are not significant and should not be interpreted.
4. **Three cells have no gradient on any day** (isolated single-cell embayments at 29.625°N/121.875°E, 31.375°N/121.625°E, 32.625°N/120.875°E). They are a negligible area but are a genuine geometric limitation of a 0.25° grid.
5. **The 2007 artifact is corrected only approximately.** The multi-scale extrapolation bounds it; it does not remove it. Trend magnitudes in the 2000s retain some residual instrument contribution.
6. **Multiple comparisons.** With ~44 series tested, some p ≈ 0.03–0.05 results (e.g. the CCF FP trend p = 0.049) would not survive a strict Bonferroni correction. The core results — Kuroshio and Subei FP (p ≤ 0.0007), the Yellow Sea onshore migration (p = 2e-7), the two-phase strength split, and the contrast collapse before 2002 — are far below any such threshold.

## Summary in one paragraph

The East China Sea carries four main SST fronts: the China Coastal Front, the Kuroshio/shelf-break front, the Subei/Jiangsu coastal front, and the Yellow Sea shelf fronts. Over 1982–2023 all four **strengthened** (annual strength trends +0.010 to +0.028 °C/100 km/yr, all p < 0.02), almost entirely in winter and spring; they also became **more seasonal**. The coastal fronts migrated **onshore** (0.17–0.45 km/yr; Yellow Sea p = 2e-7) and northeastward, while the Kuroshio front moved **offshore** — so the shelf and the deep water diverged rather than translating together. The record divides at ~2002: the first two decades saw the coastal zone warm much faster than the Kuroshio zone (+0.78 vs +0.44 °C/decade), collapsing the cross-shelf contrast (−0.34 °C/decade) and weakening every front; after 2002 the two zones warm at the same rate and the contrast is flat (p = 0.91), yet the fronts re-strengthen, so the recovery is a local cross-shore frontogenesis rather than a basin-scale contrast effect. Part of the apparent 2007 jump is the known OISST AVHRR instrument change, which the multi-scale test bounds at roughly a quarter to a third of the raw step.

# OISST East China Sea (120–128°E, 25–34°N) SST-Front Analysis, 1982–2023

## Data and method
- **Inputs:** `/inputs/0/sst` = OISST v2.1 daily SST, 15,340 files (1982-01-01→2023-12-31), 0.25° grid. `/inputs/1/ice` = same grid.
- **QC:** SST NaNs form a *static* land mask (1,012 ocean cells, 140 land cells; per-timestep NaN fraction constant 0.1215, std=0). No time-varying gaps.
- **Front detection:** Gaussian-smoothed (σ=1 cell) SST; spatial gradient magnitude |∇SST| in °C/100 km from haversine spacing; **front = |∇SST| > p90 of whole-record distribution = 3.043 °C/100 km**. Daily diagnostics: front **strength** (mean |∇SST| of front cells), **area fraction**, |∇SST|-weighted **centroid** lat/lon. Trends by **Sen slope + Mann–Kendall**.

## 1. Location of the main fronts
A persistent frontal band sits at **~28–30°N / 123–125°E** — the East China Sea shelf-break / Kuroshio shelf front (fig11 panel a; fig05). It is sharp and continuous in winter; weak, fragmented and displaced north in summer; climatological regional average gradient peaks near **29.3°N in Jan–Mar**.

## 2. Seasonality
- Front **strength**: Feb–Apr max **~3.9 °C/100 km**; Jul–Sep min **~3.4** (fig03; table_monthly_climatology.csv).
- Front **area fraction**: **0.25 (Feb–Mar)** vs **0.014–0.017 (Jul–Sep)** — ~15× seasonal swing.
- **Position**: centroid migrates **~4° north** from winter (~28.9°N) to summer (~32.3°N); latitudinal profile peak shifts from ~29.9°N (winter) to ~33.4°N (summer) (fig07). Nearly all 3,896 low-front days are Jul–Sep.

## 3. Long-term changes (1982–2023)
| Metric | Sen slope | Total/41 yr | Kendall τ | p | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Front strength** | +0.0080 °C/100 km/yr | +0.33 | +0.389 | **0.00028** | **sharpening (sig.)** |
| **Front area** | +0.0010 /yr | +0.042 | +0.310 | **0.0038** | **expansion (sig.)** |
| **Centroid latitude** | +0.0149 °N/yr | **+0.61°N** | +0.331 | **0.0020** | **northward shift (sig.)** |
| Centroid longitude | −0.0032 °E/yr | −0.13° | −0.115 | 0.28 | n.s. |
| Domain-mean \|∇SST\| | +0.0030 /yr | +0.12 | +0.187 | 0.081 | n.s. (background flat) |
| **Domain-mean SST** | +0.0301 °C/yr | **+1.23 °C** | +0.570 | **1.0e-07** | **strong warming (sig.)** |

(table_summary_all_trends.csv, fig04, fig11 panels c–d.) Spatially, 61% of ocean cells have positive |∇SST| trends and 56% are significant, concentrated on the frontal band (fig05). **Robustness:** front-strength trend persists across thresholds p80/p90/p95 (+0.0080/+0.0081/+0.0092 /yr, all p<0.001) and smoothing σ=0.5/1.5 (+0.0105/+0.0063 /yr, all p≤0.001).

## 4. Explanation
- **Strong, seasonally-uniform warming of the whole ECS:** +0.030 °C/yr overall; DJF +0.029, MAM +0.033, JJA +0.025, SON +0.026 (all p≤1e-4). Regional split S +0.027, C +0.032, N +0.030 °C/yr — no strong N–S contrast.
- **Local warming does not drive local front sharpening:** cell-wise r between local SST-warming trend and local |∇SST| trend is only **0.07** (p=0.018) (fig08).
- **Sharpening is season-selective and front-selective:**
  - Front strength: **DJF +0.0144 /yr (p=1e-5)**, **MAM +0.0104 (p=0.004)**, JJA +0.0034 (p=0.010), SON +0.0028 (n.s.) — the strongest (winter) fronts sharpen most while the domain-mean gradient stays flat.
  - Front area grows most in **DJF (+0.0027, p=0.0002)** and **MAM (+0.0014, p=0.016)**.
  - Northward centroid migration is strongest in **MAM (+0.0133°N/yr, p=0.0002)** and **JJA (+0.0219°N/yr, p=0.038)**.
- **Interpretation:** As the shelf warms, warm water extends further north in the cold season, so the winter/spring cross-shelf thermal front sharpens and its centroid migrates poleward while the diffuse summer background gradient does not strengthen. This explains why only front-selective, cold-season metrics change although basin warming is seasonally uniform.

## 5. Missing evidence / unresolved (honest)
- **The supplied `ice` dataset is effectively empty** over this box: 99.9999% NaN; only a handful of values (0.22–0.39) in Jan–Mar near the northern edge (annual ice-area trend 0.0000/yr, p=0.58; the raw monthly files contain no valid ice even in winter). **The hypothesized ice→front mechanism could not be tested and is not confirmed.**
- **No subsurface (MLD), wind-stress, river-discharge or Kuroshio-transport data** are supplied, so causal attribution (mixed-layer shoaling vs advection vs air–sea flux change) remains a hypothesis.
- Front definition uses a single fixed percentile threshold (results threshold-robust, but histogram-based edge detection not used).
- No literature-search tool or network access was provided; no external citations are made or invented.

本批次能说明与不能说明什么

OceanX保留答案更常展开定义敏感性和竞争解释，但部分最终摘要仍未吸收修正，并夸大因果排除。Claude通常提供更紧凑可用的产物链，但若干因果标题超出自身检验，且两次交付不完整。Finch在多题有有效执行工作，但本批七次尝试失败或缺执行科学证据，应先重视接入/执行问题，再讨论其普遍科研能力。这些均值只是暂定审阅读数，不证明统计显著的方法排序。
